events.name: TECHNOVA 2026 – Championship Overview
events.description: TECHNOVA 2026 is the CMS Aliganj-I Inter-House Robotics & Artificial Intelligence Championship, hosted by City Montessori School, Aliganj-I. Dates: 19 and 20 November 2026. Principal: Ms. Shivani Singh. Participants: Classes VI–XII, subject to category eligibility. Format: inter-house team and individual challenges. Reporting time: 8:00 AM on the respective event day. Help desk: Mr. Shubham Asthana. Technical coordinators: Ms. Swaranjali Rawat (8090365217) and Mr. Abhishek Sharma (9670050600).

events.name: TECHNOVA Registration
events.description: The brochure gives this registration form: https://forms.gle/YT72wa7RzUM5qmGM7 . The last date to register was 16 November 2026, which has passed as of 17 November 2026. Contact the event help desk to ask whether any late registration is possible; the brochure does not confirm late registration.

events.name: Robo Soccer
events.description: Junior category, Classes VI–VIII; 20 November 2026. Objective: score goals using a remotely controlled robot, showing control, teamwork and safe play. One robot per team, maximum 2 members. Maximum size/weight: 30 × 30 × 30 cm and 3 kg. Wired or wireless remote; autonomous functions permitted but not required. Power: maximum 12 V. Robots must not hold or trap the ball. Match: two halves of 2 minutes with a 1-minute half-time. Fouls include holding/trapping the ball for more than 5 seconds or deliberate damaging contact. Venue: Turf Area, Cambridge Section. Teacher in charge: Mr. Shantanu Kumar. Disqualification includes non-compliant robot, deliberate damage, more than three foul warnings, or unsportsmanlike conduct.

events.name: Line Follower
events.description: Junior category, Classes VI–VIII; 20 November 2026. Objective: a fully autonomous robot follows a black line on a white surface and finishes in the shortest time. Sensors: 3 individual IR sensors. Maximum size/weight: 20 × 20 × 20 cm at start and 2 kg. Onboard power source, maximum 12 V. Track includes a black line about 2–3 cm wide, straight paths, curves, intersections, and 25 × 25 cm black start/finish boxes. Team: 2 participants. Two attempts with a 1-minute gap; better time counts. Venue: Robotics Lab. Teacher in charge: Ms. Noopur Goel.

events.name: Obstacle Race
events.description: Robotics Arena; 20 November 2026. Objective: navigate an arena with a manually controlled robot and reach the finish in the shortest time. Control: wireless remote or Bluetooth. Maximum size/weight: 25 × 25 × 25 cm and 3 kg. Onboard power maximum 12 V. Possible obstacles: ramps, bridges, speed breakers, sand, stones and pebbles. Team: 2 participants. One attempt, maximum 10 minutes. Up to 3 re-entries; robot is placed at the last crossed checkpoint and the timer keeps running. Venue: Back Field. Teacher in charge: Mr. Shubham Asthana.

events.name: Robo War (Balloon Bust)
events.description: Robotics Arena; 20 November 2026. Team size: maximum 2 members. Maximum size/weight: 30 × 30 × 30 cm and 5 kg including batteries. Control: remote or Bluetooth; maximum 12 V. Wedges, scoops or hoists are permitted subject to safety inspection. Destructive/offensive weapons or systems designed to dismantle an opponent robot are prohibited. Venue: Turf Area, Cambridge Section. Teacher in charge: Ms. Swaranjali Rawat. Mandatory inspection applies. Sharp edges, projectiles, flames, hazardous substances and mechanisms likely to injure participants or spectators are prohibited.

events.name: Boat Race (Senior)
events.description: Senior only, Classes IX–XII; 20 November 2026. Teams of 2 design and operate a self-propelled model boat. Battery-operated electric motors. Maximum dimensions: length 30 cm, width 20 cm. Lightweight, waterproof and environmentally responsible materials are encouraged. Boats undergo stability and electrical safety inspection. Venue: Swimming Pool, CMS Aliganj-I. Teacher in charge: Mr. Shobhit Kanchan. Race distance, heats, lane allocation and winner-selection method will be announced at the event briefing. Do not enter the water or retrieve a boat without authorisation.

events.name: AI Model Development Challenge
events.description: AI & Computing Arena; 1 hour. Teams of 2 train a simple image, sound or gesture classifier with a beginner-friendly tool, then test it on unseen examples. Focus: data labelling, training, testing and model limitations. The brochure's AI & Computing Arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI; its detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII. Confirm eligibility with the organising team because the brochure gives both wordings. Host computers and pre-installed software are provided wherever applicable. Teacher/venue details: AI Lab; individual start time to be announced.

events.name: Computer Vision Challenge
events.description: AI & Computing Arena; 1 hour. Teams of 2 use a prepared image set and starter code (OpenCV or a pre-trained model) to detect, count or classify objects such as shapes, colours or traffic signs. Focus: image pre-processing, detection, accuracy and limitations such as lighting and blur. The arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI; detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII. Confirm eligibility with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher in charge: To be announced.

events.name: NLP Challenge
events.description: AI & Computing Arena; 1 hour. Teams of 2 work with prepared short texts, clean and tokenise them, then build a sentiment or topic classifier in Python. Focus: text pre-processing, features, evaluation and bias in language data. The arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI; detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII. Confirm eligibility with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher in charge: To be announced.

events.name: Game Development
events.description: AI & Computing Arena; 1 hour. Teams of 2 design and build a simple playable computer game on the approved platform. Judged on game logic, functionality, creativity and ability to explain the code. Detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII; the arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI, so confirm eligibility with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher in charge: Mr. Shubham Asthana.

events.name: AI & Robotics Quiz Challenge
events.description: Scheduled for 19 November 2026; 1 hour. Rounds cover robotics fundamentals, AI concepts, sensors, programming logic, applications and responsible use of AI. Round structure and scoring are explained before the quiz. Detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII; the arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI, so confirm eligibility with organisers. Venue: Computer / AI Lab. Teacher in charge: Ms. Manju Rawat. Reporting at 8:00 AM; slot to be announced.

events.name: Mini Python Chatbot
events.description: AI & Computing Arena; 1 hour. Teams of 2 build a rule-based school-helpdesk or library chatbot using strings, dictionaries, conditional statements and functions. Detailed challenge table lists Classes IX–XII; the arena heading says Senior Section, Classes IX–XI, so confirm eligibility with organisers.

events.name: AI Innovation Showdown
events.description: Senior Section, Classes IX–XI; 20 November 2026; AI Lab. Propose or demonstrate an AI-enabled solution to a meaningful real-world problem, preferably aligned with a UN Sustainable Development Goal. Entry may be a prototype, simulation or evidence-supported concept; a working demonstration is encouraged. Presentation: 8 minutes total, maximum 5 minutes presenting and 3 minutes Q&A. Components: problem statement; solution overview; AI and technical approach; impact and evidence; limitations and responsibility; future scope. Judging: problem relevance 10, technical understanding/use of AI 15, prototype/demonstration/feasibility 15, data/evidence/testing 10, originality/potential impact 5, communication/Q&A 5; total 60. Teacher in charge: Mr. Abhishek Sharma.

events.name: Student AI Challenge Guide – Six Project Ideas
events.description: The Student AI Challenge Guide introduces six short project ideas for Classes IX and XI, with suggested working time 45–60 minutes. NLP: (1) Smart Complaint Classifier—sort complaints into Transport, Library, Infrastructure, Maintenance or Canteen; (2) Suspicious Message Detector—classify sample messages as Normal, Promotional or Suspicious/Potential phishing; (3) Smart School Query Assistant—identify question intent and return approved answers. Computer Vision: (4) AI Waste Segregation Assistant—classify Plastic, Paper, Metal, Organic or Glass; (5) AI Hand Gesture Controller—recognise gestures for on-screen actions; (6) Smart Traffic Sign Recognition—classify signs such as Stop, No Entry, Speed Limit, Pedestrian Crossing or School Ahead. The organising team confirms final project option, dataset, software and permitted resources.

events.name: TECHNOVA Event Schedule
events.description: 19 November 2026: AI & Robotics Quiz Challenge, Computer / AI Lab; reporting 8:00 AM; slot to be announced. 20 November 2026: Robo Soccer, Line Follower, Obstacle Race, Robo War (Balloon Bust), Senior Boat Race, AI Innovation Showdown, Computer Vision Challenge, NLP Challenge and Game Development. Reporting 8:00 AM; event-wise venues are listed in the brochure and individual start times/heat sequences will be announced by the organising committee.

events.name: TECHNOVA Rules and General Arrangements
events.description: Teams must register under the correct class group and category before the deadline. Participants should reach the designated venue at the communicated reporting time. Bring only equipment permitted under category rules; robots and boats are subject to technical inspection. Host provides computers and pre-installed software wherever applicable. Internet, generative AI assistants, external storage and pre-written code follow category-specific instructions. Students must explain their own code, calculations, data and design decisions. Judges' decisions on scoring, safety and rule interpretation are final, subject to the announced procedure. Show respect and take care of the arena, equipment and other teams' property.

events.name: TECHNOVA Contacts
events.description: Help desk: Mr. Shubham Asthana. Technical coordinators: Ms. Swaranjali Rawat (8090365217) and Mr. Abhishek Sharma (9670050600). Event-specific teachers in charge are listed in the event details. Computer Vision Challenge and NLP Challenge teacher in charge: To be announced.

events.name: Student AI Challenge – Suggested 60-minute Plan
events.description: Suggested plan: 0–5 minutes briefing; 5–15 minutes dataset exploration; 15–35 minutes model development; 35–45 minutes testing; 45–55 minutes demonstration; 55–60 minutes explanation.

events.name: Student AI Challenge – Judging Criteria
events.description: The Student AI Challenge Guide suggests 50 marks: Problem understanding 5; Dataset preparation 10; Model development and implementation 15; Testing and prediction quality 10; Innovation and presentation 5; Explanation and understanding 5.
